questions: If moving via walkway from floor X in building (i,j) to adjacent building (i',j'), does the adjacent building need to have exactly at least X floors, or exactly X floors? The clarification says 'at least X floors', but does that mean the walkway connects floor X of the source to floor X of the destination only if the destination building's height is >= X, or does it connect to any floor >= X in the destination?

When moving via walkway, does the walkway connect the same floor number in both buildings (i.e., from floor X in source to floor X in destination), or can it connect to a different floor number in the destination building?

If the destination building has fewer than X floors, is the walkway move simply impossible, or can you take the walkway to the highest floor available (e.g., if destination has F < X, can you go to floor F)?

Can Takahashi move via walkway from floor X to an adjacent building that has exactly X floors, and then immediately use stairs within that building to adjust floor? Or must he always use stairs before/after walkway moves?

Is the cost of using a walkway always zero, or does it count toward the 'number of times that Takahashi uses stairs'? The prompt says 'count of times using stairs is incremented each time he moves up or down one floor', implying walkways are free.

If a building has height F, can Takahashi be on a floor greater than F? The constraints say Y_i ≤ F_{A_i,B_i} and Z_i ≤ F_{C_i,D_i} for start and end, but during intermediate moves, could he be on a floor > F due to walkway from a taller building?

Are walkways bidirectional? That is, if you can move from floor X in building A to adjacent building B (because B has at least X floors), can you also move from floor X in building B to building A (assuming A has at least X floors)?

If Takahashi is on floor X and wants to move to an adjacent building via walkway, but that building has height exactly X, can he later use stairs to go up within that building? Or is he stuck at floor X because it's the top floor?
